And if thou glorie: not thou beare{{ls}}t the roote, but the roote thee. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}} Thou {{ls}}aie{{ls}}t then: The boughes vvere broken, that I might be graffed in. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}} Vvel: {{sup|‖}} becau{{ls}}e of incredulitie they vvere broken, but thou by faith doe{{ls}}t {{ls}}tand: be not to highly vvi{{ls}}e, but {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We {{ls}}ee that he which {{ls}}tandeth by faith, may fall from it, and therfore mu{{ls}}t liue in feare, and not in the vaine pre{{ls}}umption and {{ls}}ecuritie of the Heretikes.}}∷ feare. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21}} For if God hath not {{ls}}pared the natural boughes: le{{ls}}t perhaps he vvil not {{ls}}pare thee neither. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22}} See then the goodnes and the {{ls}}eueritie of God: vpon them {{ls}}urely that are fallen, the {{ls}}eueritie: but vpon thee the goodnes of God, if thou abide in his goodne{{ls}}{{ls}}e, othervvi{{ls}}e thou al{{ls}}o {{ls}}halt be cut of. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=23}} But they al{{ls}}o, if they do not abide in incredulitie, {{ls}}hal be graffed in. for God is able to graffe them in againe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=24}} For if thou vva{{ls}}t cut out of the natural vvild oliue, and contrarie to nature vva{{ls}}t graffed into the good oliue: hovv much more they that are according to<noinclude>{{rh|||nature,}}</noinclude>
